title: Advancing Actionability in Oncology: Enhanced Detection of Head and Neck Cancer Recurrence
text:
Head and neck cancer imposes a significant public health burden due to the high mortality and
morbidity associated with late-stage recurrence. This project will develop an automated assay using
extracellular vesicles (EVs) and vibrational spectroscopy to detect recurrence at earlier, more
treatable stages. By enabling timely intervention and reducing reliance on invasive or inefficient
methods, the proposed technology has the potential to improve patient outcomes, extend survival,
and lessen the overall healthcare burden.

title: Gene editing therapeutics that prevent epileptic seizures
text:
--------------------------------------------------------------Project Narrative-------------------------------------------------------------
The experiments in this proposal focus on developing lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-mRNA complexes that can protect
mice from epileptic seizures via gene editing of a seizure causing gene. The LNP-mRNA complexes developed
in this proposal will edit large volumes of brain tissue non-virally and we propose to use them to treat mouse
models of seizure. If successful, the experiments in this proposal will develop a new strategy for treating seizures.

title: Incorporating geography into statistical methods for analysis of population genomic DNA
text:
A principal goal of modern human genomics is to identify the genetic variants that contribute to disease risk and to
learn about the population genetic forces that govern their prevalence and distribution. However, because global
patterns of human genetic variation are shaped by the geography of our evolutionary history, existing statistical
methods that ignore the geography of genetic variation are inadequate. To address this shortfall, we propose to
incorporate geography into new statistical methods for studying population genetic history and selection, which
together will yield new insights into human evolutionary history and the etiology of human disease.

title: Improving accessibility to multi-modal cancer image analysis and visualization through open-source software development
text:
Rapid technological advancements in cancer research have resulted in significant computational needs to
manage the large and complex datasets being generated. This project will develop free, open-source, and
sustainable computational tools to analyze and visualize high complexity datasets in the accessible and
reproducible Galaxy platform. These software tools will help researchers perform reproducible data analysis
and accelerate discoveries within early detection and personalized cancer care.

title: Research Core
text: The BBC will be designed with four major pillars in mind to assist the RPLs in their proposed studies and develop an infrastructure in bioinformatics and biostatistics for the support and capacity of the pipeline investigators and UPR researchers in the future. The goal of the BBC is to serve as an expert hub to address bioinformatics and biostatistics necessities, initially for the RPLs, but also it will serve as a training pipeline for early-stage investigators invested in cancer research. The BBC will provide infrastructure and resources to enhance the ability of investigators to develop competitive research proposals with robust research design methods, as well as high-quality scientific publications.

title: New views of the astrocyte syncytium after neonatal HI: a possible therapeutic target?
text:
Neonatal hypoxic–ischemic encephalopathy causes lifelong disability and currently lacks treatments that target
early, reversible stages of brain injury. This project develops a new MRI-based biomarker of astrocyte
dysfunction and tests an astrocyte-targeted therapy, TAT-Gap19, that may prevent secondary neuronal loss.
The results will advance early diagnosis and neuroprotective strategies for infants with hypoxic–ischemic brain
injury.

title: The genetic etiologies of stillbirth: an extreme on the developmental disorders continuum
text:
Stillbirth is a devastating pregnancy outcome that has profound emotional, psychological, and social
consequences for parents and families. This study will investigate the genetic causes of stillbirth by analyzing
the largest ever aggregated cohort of over >7,500 SB cases. Our program will comprehensively identify genetic
causes of stillbirth using new technologies and novel computational genomics methods, uncover novel genes
that are highly intolerant to genetic mutations, discover new biological mechanisms of stillbirth using in vivo
models, and enhance diagnostic screening to improve fetal health.

title: UCSF Musculoskeletal Training Program
text:
Musculoskeletal diseases, which affect more than half of the United States population age 18 and over and
nearly three-quarters age 65 and over, are among the most debilitating nonfatal health conditions. The causes
of these diseases remain poorly understood, and there is a need for better therapies. The UCSF Musculoskeletal
Training Program prepares scientists and physicians for a lifetime of scholarly pursuits that lead to in-depth
understanding and improved care for patients with MSK diseases.

title: 2026 Craniofacial Morphogenesis and Tissue Regeneration Gordon Research Conference and Gordon Research Seminar
text:
The 2026 Gordon Conference on Craniofacial Morphogenesis and Tissue Regeneration will foster cross-
disciplinary collaboration and sharing of innovative research to enhance diagnosis and therapeutics. The goal of
the conference is to advance craniofacial health by integrating genetics, model systems, and biological
mechanisms.

title: Clearance of gut derived LPS by hepatic Stabilin receptors: Mechanisms and Implications
text:
Patients with endotoxemia and other LPS associated diseases have significantly increased risk for mortality;
currently there is no specific therapy to alleviate endotoxin mediated complications in ICU patients. The aim of
this proposal is to investigate the novel innate immune functions of Stabilin receptors in liver sinusoidal endo-
thelial cells (LSEC) which clears the endotoxins and control systemic inflammation during endotoxemia. The
results from this study will provide unknown knowledge about host protective mechanism of Stabilin receptors
in LSEC and may offer potential therapeutic targets to treat several liver and LPS associated diseases.

title: Developing a novel technology for studying T cell differentiation in vivo
text:
Despite the revolutionary impact of CRISPR-based genetic screens on the study of gene functions and molecular
mechanisms in various biological processes and organisms, their application to investigate T cell differentiation
and function in physiologically relevant in vivo models remains challenging. In this proposal, the researchers aim
to address this challenge by developing a new technology that combines ribonucleoprotein complex (RNP)-
mediated gene editing with single-cell sequencing platforms. This innovative strategy will enable large-scale,
multi-module in vivo genetic screens in T cells, offering immense potential for advancing our understanding of T
cell biology and disease mechanisms.

title: JHU Center for the Advancement of HIV Neurotherapeutics (JHU CAHN) - Biomarker Core
text: The JHU Center for the Advancement of HIV Neurotherapeutics (JHU CAHN) will focus on a CNS complications that commonly present in PWH based on the framework of the NIMH Research Domain Criteria (RDoC) that classifies CNS complications based on dimensions of observable behavior and neurobiological measures that include Negative and Positive Valence Systems (e.g., anhedonia, fear), Sensorimotor Systems, Systems for Social Processes (e.g., social avoidance), Arousal/Regulatory Systems (e.g., sleep), and cognition. This framework provides new opportunities to more accurately associate biomarkers with particular symptomology with the goal of identifying molecular targets for the development of personalized medicine approaches by the Therapeutics and Clinical Cores. The Biomarker Core will work closely with the Therapeutic and Clinical cores to integrate multi-dimensional data and tools such as machine learning algorithms and offer these services to investigators interested in NeuroHIV. Technical services will include mass spectrometry analysis for metabolites, lipids, and proteins, multiplex Meso Scale discovery assays, extracellular vesicle isolation and cargo characterization. Informatics analyses offered will include Small Molecules Pathway Database, Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes, Cytoscape, and Ingenuity Pathway Analysis. Advanced non-parametric analyses will include a variety of multivariate modeling such as principal component analysis (PCA), partial least squares-discriminant analysis (PLS-DA), and sparse PLS-DA analysis, Significance analysis of metabolites (SAM), and Empirical Bayesian analysis of metabolites (EBAM) models to identify features that discriminate clinical biotypes or experimental groups. These services will be communicated broadly to the NeuroHIV community through our multicenter weekly seminar series. These services are unique to the JHU CAHN, and provide a valuable resource to NeuroHIV investigators at all stages of career development.

title: Investigating the Role of Epigenetic Regulator LSD1 in Cardiac Development
text:
Epigenetic regulators are essential for orchestrating proper embryonic development, and their disruption is
increasingly recognized as a driver of congenital heart disease (CHD). This project investigates the role of LSD1,
a histone demethylase, in cardiac development to illuminate how this important epigenetic regulator instructs
cardiac cell fate and gene regulation. Knowledge gained from this study will advance our understanding of the
molecular basis of CHD and may inform future therapeutic strategies rooted in chromatin-based regulation of
cardiac lineage specification.

title: Cellular and Genetic Defects in Keratoconus
text:
Keratoconus (KC) is a common vision-debilitating corneal dystrophy with an ill-defined polygenic basis and a
complex etiopathology. We identified poor protective antioxidant responses and gene networks that regulate
matrix and cellular functions in KC. Based on these premises, the current study will identify antioxidant
biomarkers, disease-predisposing DNA variants by next generation sequencing, and establish patient-derived
cell culture models to probe disease mechanisms and therapeutic agents.

title: Treatment of Health Complications due to Female Genital Mutilation/Cutting in Tanzania: Curriculum Build, Implementation, and Evaluation
text:
Female genital mutilation/cutting (FGM/C) affects girls and women throughout the world, with 3 million girls cut
each year, and resulting in significant reproductive, sexual, and mental health needs for impacted patients.
Implementation and evaluation of healthcare provider training programs are a top research priority to meet
these needs while also creating systemic change. This project aims to conduct a rigorous (1) needs
assessment, (2) build a training curriculum, and (3) conduct a randomized controlled trial of midwifery, nursing,
and medical students in Tanzania, a high prevalence FGM/C country.

title: A Mobile Health Intervention to Improve Psychosocial Functioning in Veterans with Posttraumatic Stress Disorder and Depression Symptoms
text:
Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and depression are the two most common mental health conditions
among Veterans. When Veterans experience both, there is a negative impact on their functioning, making it
difficult to function at work or at home and socially with other people. Although talk therapies can result in
improvements in functioning, they are difficult to access because there are limited clinicians who can provide
them. As most US adults now own a smartphone, mobile apps are a way for Veterans to access content
traditionally delivered through talk therapies at their own pace. The proposed study will build and test a mobile
app based on a trauma-informed talk therapy that has helped Veterans with PTSD and depression make large
improvements in functioning, through learning skills to navigate emotions and relationships. Additionally,
through answering brief surveys and enabling passive tracking on their smartphones, Veterans will see real-
time information on their functioning and mental health and on potential benefits from using these skills.

title: Center for Modeling Non-Coding Disease Variants: Disease Modeling Project
text: DISEASE MODELING PROJECT The aim of Disease Modeling Core is to advance our understanding of non-coding disease variants by generating and disseminating knock-in mouse models. This project addresses a critical gap in genomic research by focusing on the functional characterization of variants affecting non-coding regulatory elements, such as enhancers, silencers, alternative promoters and others, which play crucial roles in gene expression regulation and disease pathogenesis. The core will employ a novel dual-enSERT transgenic technology to classify non-coding variants as CIS or TRANS regulatory elements. This classification is essential for subsequent knock-in analysis and will help prioritize variants for further study. Over the grant period, the core aims to create transgenic and knock-in models for approximately 100 prioritized variants, encompassing various regulatory types to maximize the identification of functional variants and broaden the scope of the study. In Aim 1, the core will utilize a unique dual-enSERT transgenic technology to assess wild-type and variant cis-regulatory activity in live mice simultaneously. This approach will help establish the functional significance of disease variants within enhancer regions and inform subsequent knock-in studies. In Aim 2 we will generate a panel of disease variant knock-in mice to determine the in vivo functional significance of prioritized non-coding variants and provide a valuable resource for the scientific community. These models will undergo standardized phenotyping, including gene expression analysis, anatomical and pathological assessments, and integration with patient-derived data. The Disease Modeling Core will collaborate closely with the Bioinformatics Core, which will prioritize active non- coding variants for modeling. Additionally, the core will work with the Service Core to ensure efficient distribution of the variant knock-in mouse models. This project represents a significant step forward in bridging technology and physiology to tackle one of the most challenging quests of the genomic era: identifying non-coding variants that "matter" in a sea of potential ones. By focusing on active and conserved variants and employing innovative in vivo screening techniques, the Disease Modeling Core aims to provide crucial insights into the mechanistic and physiological roles of non-coding variants in disease. The resulting mouse models and associated data will serve as a valuable resource for researchers studying various diseases and will contribute to our understanding of gene regulation and disease pathogenesis.

title: Testing Multi-Level Remote Physical Activity Interventions in a National Sample of Older Women: The WHISH EnCore Trial
text: While older women are disproportionately affected by chronic diseases that can be alleviated by regular physical activity, few physical activity programs have been developed specifically with their needs in mind. Those programs that are available typically do not address the recognized local contextual factors that can impact physical activity. This research aims to evaluate the added effects on one-year physical activity levels of a novel citizen science neighborhood engagement program (called Our Voice) when combined with a remotely-delivered “light touch” physical activity program with participants from the Women’s Health Initiative Strong & Healthy (WHISH) trial, relative to the remotely delivered individually-focused program alone. The programs represent a potentially scalable means for promoting physical activity across broad groups of US older women.

title: Accelerating the expert-crowdsourcing of cancer variant interpretation in CIViC
text:
The Clinical Interpretation of Variants in Cancer (CIViC) knowledgebase is a widely adopted, open access,
community-driven web resource created to centralize and standardize expert-curated cancer variant
interpretations to aid precision oncology. This proposal will build on the success of the CIViC project by
developing and implementing several new features to improve user experience, biocuration and moderation
through automation of variant pathogenicity or oncogenicity classification, supporting journal submissions,
creating an editor tool box for increased efficiency, development of new natural language processing tools for
fact-checking and annotating evidence, and increasing education and outreach to support editor recruiting,
training and incentivization. These advances will move us closer to our ultimate goal of having every tumor
sequencing test that predicts somatic variants being evaluated against the CIViC knowledgebase for potential
oncogenicity or clinical significance.

title: Overcoming Immune Checkpoint Blockade Resistance in Glioblastoma with a Novel Stem Cell Biotherapeutic
text:
The proposed combination therapy addresses a vital unmet need for patients with recurrent glioblastoma and
other advanced cancers that are resistant to PD-1 blockade therapy. Our therapeutic platform aims to
significantly expand the clinical benefits of immunotherapy to a larger patient population by reversing their
resistance to PD-1 inhibition therapy. Ultimately, our platform is poised to synergize with various
immunotherapies, serving as an essential adjunct and sensitizer for diverse cancers and combination
treatments.
